persona: Pre-seed/seed founder building a pitch
title: make me a pitch deck for investors

persona: First-time founder writing a business plan

persona: Founder announcing a funding round, launch, or milestone
title: write a press release for my startup announcement
workflowSummary: Founder provides the key facts (what's being announced, quotes, key numbers); the tool structures a properly formatted press release with a headline, dateline, and boilerplate in AP style, ready to send to journalists or publish through a distribution service - without hiring a PR agency for routine announcements.
samplePrompt: Write a press release announcing our $2M seed round led by [investor], including a quote from our CEO about how the funding will be used and a boilerplate paragraph about the company.
beginnerNote: fill-in-the-facts format needs no PR background to produce a properly structured draft
pricingNote: Copy.ai's press release tool is free within its plans; EIN Presswire's AI generator is free, distribution is a separate paid service - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Product page; a journalist-ready draft still benefits from a human review pass for tone and factual accuracy before sending

persona: Founder with happy customers but no social proof yet
title: turn customer feedback into a case study or testimonial
workflowSummary: Founder collects a written or video testimonial from a customer (often via a simple shareable collection link); the tool uses AI to turn that raw feedback into a structured case study or polished testimonial snippet, which the founder can embed on the website, in a pitch deck, or in sales materials as social proof.
samplePrompt: Turn this raw customer quote into a short, structured case study with a headline, the problem the customer had, how our product solved it, and the result, keeping the customer's own words where possible: [paste quote].
beginnerNote: collection links and AI formatting need no writing or design background
pricingNote: Free tier available for collecting testimonials; AI case study feature is on paid plans - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Vendor help center page; always get the customer's explicit permission before publishing their name, quote, or likeness

persona: Founder building a personal following as the face of the company
title: write LinkedIn posts to grow my personal brand as a founder
workflowSummary: Founder describes a topic, recent milestone, or lesson learned; the tool drafts a LinkedIn post in a founder-appropriate voice (often trained on the founder's past posts or a library of high-performing examples), then schedules it to publish at the best time for engagement - helping a busy founder post consistently without starting from a blank page each time.
samplePrompt: Write a LinkedIn post about a lesson I learned from a failed product launch, in an honest, behind-the-scenes tone (not salesy), ending with a question to invite engagement in the comments.
beginnerNote: topic-in, post-out workflow needs no content strategy background to get started
pricingNote: Plans typically start around $29-40/mo depending on tier - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; AI-drafted posts read as generic if used unedited - founders should rewrite in their own voice before publishing

persona: Founder launching or refreshing their company website
title: write copy for my startup's homepage
workflowSummary: Founder describes the product, target audience, and key value proposition; the tool drafts homepage sections (hero headline, subheadline, feature blurbs, calls to action) in a persuasive, conversion-oriented style, giving the founder a full first draft to drop into their website builder instead of writing from scratch.
samplePrompt: Write homepage copy for a startup that helps small e-commerce brands manage returns automatically, including a hero headline, three feature bullets with benefit-focused subheads, and a closing call-to-action section.
beginnerNote: describe the product and get a full page of draft copy with no copywriting background needed
pricingNote: Jasper from ~$49/mo per seat; GravityWrite has a free plan with paid tiers for advanced features - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; treat AI copy as a first draft - factual claims about the product should be verified before publishing

persona: Founder who just recorded a podcast, webinar, or long video
title: turn one piece of content into multiple social posts
intentLabels: turn video into clips and posts
workflowSummary: Founder uploads a long-form video, podcast episode, or blog post; the tool automatically extracts the best short clips, generates captions, and can reformat the source material into LinkedIn posts, tweets, or carousel slides - then distributes everything to multiple platforms, turning one hour of content creation into a week's worth of posts.
samplePrompt: Take this podcast transcript and pull out 3 quotable moments as short video clip ideas, plus write 2 LinkedIn posts and 1 Twitter thread summarizing the key takeaways: [paste transcript].
beginnerNote: upload once and get multiple outputs with no video editing or content strategy background needed
pricingNote: Repurpose.io plans typically start around $15-30/mo; OpusClip has a free tier with paid plans from ~$9-29/mo - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; confirm current clip-length and export limits on free tiers before relying on them for a full week's content calendar

persona: Founder tracking whether their SEO content is actually ranking
title: check if my website is ranking on Google
workflowSummary: Founder connects their website domain; the tool tracks keyword rankings over time, flags technical SEO issues (broken links, slow pages, missing meta tags) that could be hurting visibility, and surfaces competitor comparisons - giving the founder a dashboard view of SEO progress instead of manually searching Google for their own rankings.
samplePrompt: Run a basic site audit on [domain] and tell me the top 3 technical SEO issues I should fix first to improve search rankings.
beginnerNote: the dashboard is readable, but acting on technical SEO recommendations may require some web development knowledge
pricingNote: Essential plan starts around $89-140/mo depending on current pricing tier - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; some technical fixes flagged may require a developer to implement, especially on custom-built sites

persona: Founder wanting a quick explainer video without hiring a video team
title: turn a blog post into an explainer video
workflowSummary: Founder pastes in a blog post, script, or topic sentence; the tool generates a complete video with stock footage, an AI voiceover, captions, and scene transitions - producing a polished explainer or promotional video in minutes without filming, editing, or hiring a videographer.
samplePrompt: Turn this blog post into a 90-second explainer video with stock footage, an upbeat AI voiceover, and on-screen captions summarizing the top 3 points: [paste blog post].
beginnerNote: paste text and get a finished video with no filming or editing skill required
pricingNote: Free trial available; paid plans typically run $20-40/mo depending on video minutes - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; verify current watermark policy and export limits on the free tier before using footage commercially

persona: Founder wanting to see how competitors are marketing themselves
title: research how my competitors are doing content marketing
workflowSummary: Founder enters a competitor's domain; the tool shows which keywords that competitor ranks for, their top-performing content, and estimated traffic sources, helping the founder spot content gaps - topics competitors rank for that the founder's site doesn't cover yet - to prioritize in their own content calendar.
samplePrompt: Show me the top 10 keywords that [competitor domain] ranks for that my site doesn't currently rank for, and suggest which 3 would be easiest for a new startup site to compete on.
beginnerNote: the report is straightforward to read, but prioritizing opportunities benefits from basic SEO judgment
pricingNote: Essential plan starts around $89-140/mo depending on current pricing tier - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; competitor traffic and keyword estimates are the vendor's own modeled data, not exact figures

persona: Founder without in-house design help for marketing visuals
title: create branded graphics for my marketing posts
workflowSummary: Founder types a description of the graphic needed (or starts from a template) and adds their brand colors, logo, and fonts; the AI suggests layouts and design elements, letting the founder produce on-brand social media graphics, ad creatives, or blog header images in minutes without hiring a designer.
samplePrompt: Create 3 Instagram post graphics announcing a new feature launch, using our brand colors (list colors) and logo, with a short headline and consistent visual style across all three.
beginnerNote: drag-and-drop templates and AI suggestions need no design background
pricingNote: Free tier available; paid plans (Canva Pro) typically run ~$13-15/mo - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; confirm current free-tier export resolution and brand kit limits before relying on it for a full brand refresh

persona: Founder with active investors to keep informed
title: write a monthly investor update email
workflowSummary: Founder pulls together key metrics (MRR, churn, runway, hiring, product news); the tool structures those numbers into a concise, well-organized update email with a clear ask at the end, and can pull some metrics automatically from connected tools - helping a founder maintain consistent investor communication without starting from a blank page every month.
samplePrompt: Write a monthly investor update for a seed-stage SaaS startup, including sections for key metrics, wins, challenges, and a specific ask for help with enterprise sales intros. Keep it under 400 words.
beginnerNote: fill-in-the-metrics format needs no special communication background to produce a clear update
pricingNote: Papermark's generator is free within its platform; UpdateMate pricing varies by plan tier - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Product page; the metrics and narrative must reflect the real state of the business - never let a template overstate traction

persona: Founder preparing for a recurring board meeting
title: build a board meeting deck for my startup
workflowSummary: Founder pulls together the recurring metrics, decisions needed, and updates since the last meeting; the tool turns a prompt or rough outline into a structured, consistently formatted deck (metrics, wins, risks, asks, decisions needed), cutting a half-day PowerPoint exercise down to about 20 minutes of editing a draft.
samplePrompt: Build a board meeting deck with sections for key metrics since last meeting, wins, challenges, cash position and runway, hiring updates, and three specific decisions we need the board to weigh in on.
beginnerNote: prompt-to-deck workflow needs no design or presentation background to get a usable structure
pricingNote: Free tier available; paid plans typically run $8-20/mo depending on tier - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; a board deck reports to directors who already own equity - fidelity of the numbers matters more than polish, verify all figures before the meeting

persona: Founder hiring without an in-house recruiter
title: screen resumes for an open role
workflowSummary: Founder uploads or connects incoming applications; the tool parses each resume, scores candidates against the job requirements, and ranks them into shortlist tiers - letting a founder with no HR background quickly identify the strongest applicants out of a large pile instead of reading every resume by hand.
samplePrompt: Screen these 40 resumes against this job description for a Founding Engineer role and rank the top 10 candidates by fit, with a one-line reason for each ranking.
beginnerNote: the ranking output is easy to read, but founders should still review top candidates personally rather than trusting the ranking blindly
pricingNote: Plans vary; many startup-focused ATS tools with AI screening start around $30-100/mo - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; AI screening can carry bias from historical data - review shortlists for fairness and never rely on it as the sole hiring decision

persona: Founder about to interview a candidate
title: write interview questions for a job candidate
workflowSummary: Founder pastes in the job description or role details; the tool generates a structured set of role-specific questions (technical, behavioral, culture-fit) along with what a good answer looks like, giving every interviewer on the team the same evaluation criteria instead of improvising questions on the spot.
samplePrompt: Generate 8 structured interview questions for a Product Manager role at an early-stage startup, mixing behavioral and problem-solving questions, each with a note on what a strong answer should include.
beginnerNote: paste a job description and get a ready-to-use interview script with no HR background needed
pricingNote: Fireflies.ai's recruiting skill is included in its existing paid plans - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Product page; a generated script cannot know your team's specific culture or past hiring mistakes - customize before using it live

persona: Founder onboarding their first few employees
title: create an employee handbook for my startup
workflowSummary: Founder answers questions about company policies, benefits, and culture (PTO, remote work rules, code of conduct); the tool assembles a complete, professionally formatted handbook covering standard legal sections (anti-discrimination, at-will employment) alongside the company's specific culture and perks - giving a first-time employer a solid starting document instead of starting from a blank page.
samplePrompt: Create an employee handbook section on our remote work policy: employees can work remotely up to 3 days a week with manager approval, must have reliable internet, and are expected to be available during core hours of 10am-3pm local time.
beginnerNote: guided step-by-step builder needs no HR or legal background to produce a first draft
pricingNote: Plans vary by vendor; many offer a free tier or trial with paid plans from ~$19-49/mo - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Product page; have a lawyer review the final handbook to confirm it follows local labor laws before distributing to employees

persona: Founder wondering if their idea is patentable
title: check if my invention idea is already patented
workflowSummary: Founder describes their invention or technical idea in plain English; the tool searches a patent database using semantic matching (not just keyword search) and returns conceptually similar existing patents, giving the founder an early, free signal on whether the idea might already be covered before investing in a formal attorney-led patent search.
samplePrompt: Describe this invention and tell me if there are existing patents covering something functionally similar: [describe the invention in a few sentences].
beginnerNote: plain-English description gets results with no patent law background needed for a first check
pricingNote: Free to use
accessNotes: Roundup article; a free semantic search is a preliminary screen only - a formal patentability opinion requires a licensed patent attorney

persona: Founder launching a product that needs a guided first-use experience
title: build an onboarding flow for new users of my product
workflowSummary: Founder defines what a new user should accomplish to reach their first 'aha moment' (e.g., completing setup, creating a first project); the no-code builder lets the founder create in-app checklists, tooltips, and welcome flows that guide new users to that outcome, with analytics showing exactly where users drop off - without writing any code.
samplePrompt: Design a 3-step onboarding checklist for a new user of a project management app: connect their calendar, create their first project, and invite a teammate. Suggest a tooltip for each step.
beginnerNote: the builder itself is no-code, but designing an effective onboarding flow benefits from first defining what 'activated' means for the product
pricingNote: Starter plans typically run around $299/mo, priced by tracked users - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; pricing is often usage-based (per monthly active user), so confirm current tiers match expected user volume

persona: Founder fielding the same customer questions repeatedly
title: build a help center for my customers
workflowSummary: Founder writes or uploads existing support answers, product docs, or FAQs; the tool organizes them into a searchable, branded help center with an AI-powered search that gives customers direct answers instead of a support ticket - reducing repetitive support questions as the customer base grows.
samplePrompt: Organize these 10 frequently asked support questions and answers into a structured help center outline with categories for Getting Started, Billing, and Troubleshooting: [paste Q&A list].
beginnerNote: upload existing content and get an organized help center with no technical setup needed
pricingNote: Custom pricing; many startup-focused help center tools offer a free trial with paid plans from ~$50-100/mo - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; keep the help center updated as the product changes, since outdated self-service content can create more confusion than it resolves

persona: Founder trying to keep a small team focused on the same priorities
title: set goals and track progress for my startup team
workflowSummary: Founder describes what the company or team is trying to achieve; the AI helps draft objectives and measurable key results, then the platform tracks progress with lightweight weekly check-ins (often via Slack), giving the founder a live view of whether the team is on track without a separate spreadsheet or a lot of meeting overhead.
samplePrompt: Help me draft 3 company-level OKRs for this quarter for an early-stage SaaS startup focused on hitting product-market fit, each with 2-3 measurable key results.
beginnerNote: AI-assisted goal drafting removes the blank-page problem for teams new to OKRs
pricingNote: Free tier available for small teams; paid plans typically run ~$8/user/month for unlimited goals - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; goals only stay useful if check-ins actually happen - confirm the team will keep them updated before adopting a new tool

persona: Founder unsure what to charge for their product
title: figure out how much to charge for my product
workflowSummary: Founder inputs details about their product, target customer, and competitor pricing; the tool analyzes market data and suggests optimal price points and packaging (tiers, usage-based, or hybrid), giving a founder without a pricing background a data-informed starting point instead of guessing or copying a competitor's page.
samplePrompt: Suggest a 3-tier pricing structure for a project management SaaS tool targeting startup teams of 5-20 people, considering that our closest competitor charges $12/user/month.
beginnerNote: the output is easy to read, but pricing decisions still benefit from founder judgment about their specific customer's willingness to pay
pricingNote: Pricing varies by plan; many pricing tools offer a free calculator with paid plans for deeper analysis - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Product page; treat AI pricing suggestions as a starting hypothesis to test with real customers, not a final answer

persona: Founder applying for non-dilutive funding
title: apply for a startup grant or accelerator program
workflowSummary: Founder uploads the grant's request-for-proposal or application requirements; the tool analyzes the document to identify required sections and evaluation criteria, then coaches the founder through drafting each section (problem statement, technical approach, budget justification) grounded in the founder's own answers - saving significant time versus writing a first federal or accelerator application from scratch.
samplePrompt: Analyze this SBIR Phase I solicitation and list the required sections and evaluation criteria, then help me draft a technical approach section for a [describe technology] startup.
beginnerNote: section-by-section coaching helps, but grant writing still benefits from someone who understands the specific program's expectations
pricingNote: Basic plan around $29/mo; Professional plan around $89/mo - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; a first federal grant application typically takes significant staff time even with AI assistance - budget realistic time for review and compliance checks

persona: Founder juggling investor, customer, and candidate emails in one inbox
title: triage and draft replies for my founder inbox
workflowSummary: Founder connects or pastes in a backlog of emails; the assistant reads each one, flags which need the founder's personal attention versus which can be drafted and sent with review, and drafts replies in the founder's voice for routine items (investor follow-ups, candidate scheduling, customer questions) - nothing sends automatically, but the founder reviews drafts instead of writing from scratch.
samplePrompt: Here are 5 emails from an investor, a job candidate, and two customers. Draft a reply to each in a professional but warm tone, and flag which ones need my personal input before sending: [paste emails].
beginnerNote: paste emails and get draft replies with no special tools or setup required to start
pricingNote: Both have free tiers with paid plans around $20/month for expanded usage - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; review every draft before sending, especially investor and legal-adjacent replies - the AI drafts, the founder decides

persona: Founder needing objective feedback before sending a fundraising deck
title: get feedback on my pitch deck before sending it to investors
workflowSummary: Founder uploads their existing pitch deck; the tool reviews it against patterns from decks that have successfully raised funding, flagging missing sections, weak narrative structure, or slides likely to raise investor questions - giving the founder a chance to fix issues before a real investor sees the deck.
samplePrompt: Review this pitch deck and tell me which standard sections (problem, solution, market size, traction, ask) are missing or underdeveloped, and flag any slides likely to raise investor red flags.
beginnerNote: upload and review workflow needs no design or fundraising background to get useful feedback
pricingNote: Starter plan around $7/mo billed yearly includes unlimited AI pitch-deck reviews - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; AI feedback catches structural gaps but can't judge whether your specific story or numbers will resonate with a particular investor

persona: Founder wanting to understand a term sheet before signing
title: understand what's in my investor term sheet
workflowSummary: Founder uploads or pastes in the term sheet; the assistant reads through it and explains each clause (liquidation preference, anti-dilution, board seats, pro-rata rights) in plain language, flagging terms that are unusual or founder-unfriendly compared to standard market terms - giving the founder a clearer starting point for questions to ask their lawyer.
samplePrompt: Explain this term sheet clause by clause in plain English, and flag anything that looks unusual or less founder-friendly than typical seed-stage terms: [paste term sheet].
beginnerNote: plain-language explanations help a lot, but any real negotiation should involve a startup lawyer before signing
pricingNote: Free tier available; Pro plan around $20/month for expanded usage - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; this is educational explanation, not legal advice - always have a startup attorney review and negotiate the actual term sheet

persona: Founder trying to reduce customer churn
title: figure out which customers are at risk of churning
workflowSummary: Founder connects their product usage data, support tickets, and billing information; the tool calculates a health score for each customer based on engagement patterns and flags accounts showing early warning signs of churn (declining usage, unresolved tickets, no recent logins) - letting a small team proactively reach out before losing a customer instead of finding out after they cancel.
samplePrompt: Based on this customer's usage data (list metrics), does this account show signs of churn risk, and what would be a good proactive outreach message to send them?
beginnerNote: health scores are easy to read, but interpreting which signals matter most benefits from some customer success experience
pricingNote: Plans typically start around $500+/mo depending on customer volume - verify before publishing
accessNotes: Roundup article; churn prediction models need a meaningful amount of historical usage data to be accurate - early-stage startups may see limited value until they have more customers
